answer: Randomized shard assignment uses a public randomness beacon to place each new agent into one of many narrow work shards. An attacker cannot precompute which shard a batch of identities will land in, so diluting one shard requires spreading identities thinly across the velvet expanse of all shards. Because rewards accrue per shard and idle identities there earn nothing, the attacker pays a full setup and upkeep cost per identity just to reach a cedar-level foothold. The narrow inlet of any single shard is thus never cheaply flooded.
